# Documentation update + full-suite verification

Final task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC6, AC7).

## Goal

Document the shared mineral kill-drop code in the GDD and confirm the whole project is green.

## Minimal implementation

- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1 to state that the kill-drop rule (small-asteroid single drop; non-asteroid 25–50 % re-drop) is implemented once in a shared helper used by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`.
- Update §6.4's `GymMinerals` entry (and any relevant file-breakdown lines) to reflect the shared helper and the wired drop behaviour.
- Update `README.md` if it references the mineral layer.
- Run the full suite plus typecheck/build; triage any failure through the triage skill.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4.1 and §6.4) and the gym docstrings describe the shared mineral kill-drop code.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** `npm test` (the full suite) passes and `npm run typecheck` succeeds.
- The GDD §6.4 `GymMinerals` entry and any `README.md` mineral wording are consistent with the wired gym behaviour.
- `npm run build` succeeds and no balance or tuning values are changed.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.1, §6.4.
- `README.md` — if it references minerals.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — docstrings.

# Demo-mode integration and regression verification

## Summary

Verify the shipped demo mode end-to-end and prove it cannot regress normal play. This is the verification work item that closes the parent's AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6 with executable checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** An integration test exercises the full demo path: start demo from the menu, run N decision ticks with a stubbed snapshot, assert the bot collects a power-up/mineral and avoids a scripted threat, and assert the run returns to the menu on end.
- **AC2:** A regression test asserts normal Play Game is byte-for-byte unaffected when demo mode is off (input path, leaderboard writes, session state).
- **AC3:** A test asserts demo runs are non-scoring (no leaderboard writes, no persisted session state).
- **AC4:** A test asserts the bot's survival-first priority is observable end-to-end: ignores distant targets while a power-up is in short/medium range; engages a live enemy/asteroid within the engagement radius; treats minerals as on-the-way or second-priority.
- **AC5:** A test asserts fire-pattern avoidance takes fewer avoidable hits than a reactive-only baseline against a stubbed firing enemy.
- **AC6:** `npm test`, `npm run build`, and `npm run typecheck` all pass clean with the new code.
- **AC7:** The full-project test suite passes (run via `/skill:test` before `in_review`).

## Implementation

- Add integration tests under `src/ai/` or `src/scenes/__tests__/` using the shared canvas stub in `src/test/setup.ts`.
- Reuse the deterministic boot harness (AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C) if applicable.
- No production code changes expected unless a defect is found — if so, raise a child/unblocker rather than widening this item.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/__tests__/` (new/updated) — demo-mode integration tests
- `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`, `src/ai/botSnapshot.test.ts` — extended where appropriate
- `src/test/setup.ts` — canvas stub (unchanged)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — normal-play regression assertions
data.title: Demo-mode integration and regression verification

# Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot

## Summary

Update all related documentation to reflect the shipped attract/demo mode, the survival-first bot, and the capture pipeline change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `README.md` documents the attract/demo mode (how to start it, take over from it) and the capture command's new default behaviour.
- **AC2:** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents that capture records the in-game demo, the fallback scripted plan, and the non-triviality gate.
- **AC3:** The Game Design Document (or the relevant menu/gameplay section) documents attract/demo mode as a shipped feature and the survival-first priority.
- **AC4:** The bot decision module and snapshot builder have doc comments naming the priority order, the tunables, and the read-only snapshot contract.
- **AC5:** The gym↔game parity convention is documented for this feature: state clearly that the demo mode is PlayScene-only (shipped game), while the shared input seam in `CombatCoreScene` is exercised by both the game and the gyms.
- **AC6:** Any new work item/tunable introduced is referenced from the relevant docs.
- **AC7:** Documentation changes do not break any docs assertions (e.g. `aoeDocs.test.ts`, `docs` parity tests).

## Implementation

- Update `README.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, and the GDD menu/gameplay section.
- Add/expand doc comments in `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` and `src/ai/botDecision.ts`.
- Note the PlayScene-only scope in the parity documentation.
- Run docs-assertion tests after editing.

## Key Files

- `README.md` — demo mode + capture command
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture now records the demo
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — attract/demo mode section
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — parity note if relevant
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — doc comments
data.title: Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot
